info.name: Restful Booker API
info.description:
Portfolio demo collection for the public Restful Booker API.

Run the folders in order. Later requests reuse the token and booking ids saved by earlier ones.

Username and password default to the public demo credentials published by that API (admin / password123).

Generated from scripts/collection.js. Edit that file, then run npm run build.

item.name: 01 Health
item.description: Liveness check. GET /ping returns 201 and the plain text Created.

item.name: Ping
item.description: Confirms the demo process is accepting requests before the suite creates anything.

exec: pm.test("content type is plain text", function () {
pm.test("body reports the service is up", function () {

item.name: 02 Authentication
item.description: Creates the token write requests send as a Cookie, then checks that a bad password and a non-JSON content type do not issue a token or replace the saved one. A failed login is HTTP 200 with reason Bad credentials.

item.name: Create token
item.description: POST /auth with the public demo username and password. Saves the token for later writes.

exec: pm.test("body matches the token schema", function () {
pm.test("token is saved for chained write requests", function () {

item.name: Reject bad credentials
item.description: Same user, wrong password. The saved token from Create token must stay in place.

exec: pm.test("body matches the auth error schema", function () {
pm.test("failed login does not replace the saved token", function () {
pm.test("failed login response has no token", function () {

item.name: Reject non-JSON login
item.description: The demo treats a login that is not application/json as bad credentials, even when the body is the right JSON text.

exec: pm.test("body matches the auth error schema", function () {
pm.test("failed login does not replace the saved token", function () {
pm.test("failed login response has no token", function () {

item.name: 03 Booking lifecycle
item.description: One booking, created with a unique name, then read, filtered, replaced, partially updated, and deleted. Later requests use the id and token saved above. Writes send an unknown clientRef field, which must not be stored.

item.name: Create booking
item.description: POST /booking. No token is required to create. Saves bookingId.

exec: // Unique first name so this run does not collide with other users of the public demo.
pm.test("body matches the created-booking schema", function () {
pm.test("booking id is saved for chained requests", function () {
pm.test("created booking echoes the request and drops clientRef", function () {

item.name: Get booking
item.description: GET /booking/:id. The stored document must match the create payload.

exec: pm.test("bookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("body matches the booking schema", function () {
pm.test("stored booking matches the create payload", function () {

item.name: Find booking by name
item.description: GET /booking?firstname&lastname. The filter must return this run's id and not the full dataset.

exec: pm.test("bookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("body matches the booking id list schema", function () {
pm.test("filtered ids include the created booking and not the whole dataset", function () {

item.name: Replace booking
item.description: PUT /booking/:id with the Cookie token. Replaces every field.

exec: // Values the next response must echo.
pm.test("token was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("bookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("body matches the booking schema", function () {
pm.test("replacement echoes the new payload and drops clientRef", function () {

item.name: Confirm replaced booking
item.description: Read-after-write. The replacement must be what a later GET returns, not only what PUT echoed.

exec: pm.test("bookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("body matches the booking schema", function () {
pm.test("stored booking matches the replacement", function () {

item.name: Patch additional needs
item.description: PATCH /booking/:id changes additionalneeds only. Price, dates, and name must stay at the replaced values.

exec: // Values the next response must echo.
pm.test("token was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("bookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("body matches the booking schema", function () {
pm.test("partial update changes additionalneeds and keeps the other fields", function () {

item.name: Confirm patched booking
item.description: Read-after-write for the partial update.

exec: pm.test("bookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("body matches the booking schema", function () {
pm.test("stored booking matches the partial update", function () {

exec: pm.test("token was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("bookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {

exec: pm.test("bookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("content type is plain text", function () {

item.name: 04 Negative cases
item.description: Authorization failures, unknown ids, malformed creates, and a characterization of the missing stay-date check. Bookings created here are deleted before the folder ends.

item.name: Create booking with empty body
item.description: POST /booking {}. The demo responds with a plain-text 500 rather than a structured 400.

exec: pm.test("content type is plain text", function () {
pm.test("body is Internal Server Error", function () {

item.name: Create booking missing firstname
item.description: A payload without firstname is also a plain-text 500.

exec: pm.test("content type is plain text", function () {
pm.test("body is Internal Server Error", function () {

item.name: Create booking with inverted dates
item.description: Checkout is before checkin. The demo accepts the stay and echoes the dates. This locks that gap so a future validation change fails the suite on purpose.

exec: // Unique first name so this run does not collide with other users of the public demo.
pm.test("body matches the created-booking schema", function () {
pm.test("booking id is saved for chained requests", function () {
pm.test("inverted dates are echoed and clientRef is dropped", function () {
pm.test("checkout before checkin is currently accepted", function () {

item.name: Delete inverted-date booking
item.description: Removes the characterization booking so the shared demo is not left with it.

exec: pm.test("token was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.test("edgeBookingId was chained from an earlier request", function () {
pm.expect(pm.collectionVariables.get("edgeBookingId"), "Run Create booking with inverted dates first.").to.match(/^[0-9]+$/);
